_doc: T032 LEGAL gov-oracle (TT-478). Each case asserts that the Catala-computed IHT death charge equals the AUTHORITATIVE published gov.uk figure cited inline — not just a structurally-valid shape. scripts/oracle_verify.py runs the rule's scope with `inputs` and requires the Computed-arm money to equal `expected_money_gbp`; a mismatch (e.g. a wrong rule literal) turns the harness RED. Figures sourced from gov.uk on `sourced_at` and must be re-verified against the live page if edited (HALT fork 2: never assert a tax figure from memory).
statute: IHTA 1984 s.7 + Schedule 1 (death-charge rate); s.8D–s.8E (residence nil-rate band, FA 2015)

cases.label: v1-no-home-500k
cases.citation_quote: Your estate is worth £500,000 and your tax-free threshold is £325,000. The Inheritance Tax charged will be 40% of £175,000 (£500,000 minus £325,000).

cases.label: v2-home-to-descendants-500k
cases.citation_quote: If you own your home (or a share in it) your tax-free threshold can increase to £500,000 if: you leave it to your children (including adopted, foster or stepchildren) or grandchildren
cases.note: Threshold £325,000 + RNRB min(£200,000, £175,000) = £500,000; estate £500,000 ≤ £500,000 → £0. Quote refreshed 2026-07-11 (TT-883) after gov.uk reworded the passing-on-home page; no-substance determination: £500,000 threshold + closely-inherited-by-descendants eligibility unchanged (FA 2015 s.8D–8E), only wording restructured.

cases.label: v3-taper-2_1m
cases.citation_quote: The residence nil rate band will reduce by £1 for every £2 that the estate is worth more than the £2 million taper threshold.
cases.note: Estate £2.1m exceeds £2m by £100k → RNRB taper −£50k → RNRB £125k; threshold £450k; (£2,100,000 − £450,000) × 40% = £660,000.
